about: A / in JS or TS starts a regex literal or divides, by the token before it. A tokenizer that guesses division where a regex starts reads a regex's \/ and closing / as //, takes the rest of the line for a comment, and a lint reading the code drops what is written there. The rule: after the ) of an if, while, for or with head, a / starts a regex; after any other ), after ], ++, --, a word, a number, a string, a template or a regex, it divides (after a postfix ++ or -- the expression is complete, and a prefix one cannot take a regex); after (, [, a comma, an operator, ;, :, {, the } of a block, or a keyword such as return or typeof, it starts a regex. Where the tokenizer cannot decide (a ) or } whose opener it has not seen or cannot classify), it scans both readings and keeps the union of what each reads as code, so it fails closed.
rows: each source, as a whole file read as TSX (a .tsx file: TypeScript with JSX), and whether the unsafe text after the slash is code (hit) or a comment.

generate: regex_line over regex_before and undecided_before x bodies is always a hit; division_line over division_before is never one, and over undecided_before always one (the union). Run by manaflow-ai/cmux-platform test/node/no-guessable-temp-names.test.ts; written so any other hand-rolled JS tokenizer (manaflow-ai/cmux scripts/check-test-determinism.py) can run it as is, where a case its lexer reports as unresolved counts as failing closed.

rows.why: the ) of a for await head
the outer ) is the if head's, past nested calls
after [
after (
after ?
after return
after the } of a block
a ) that closes nothing seen: both readings are scanned and their union reported
a } whose { followed a colon (a label's block or an object literal's value): both readings
after a postfix ++ the expression is complete: a / divides
after a postfix --, a / divides
fails closed: where the reading is undecided, the regex reading keeps the text a division reading would drop
after the ) of a call, a / divides and // is a comment
after ], a / divides
after the } of an object literal, a / divides
a keyword after . is a property name
after the ) of a group

inside a JSX open tag, the / after an attribute's or a spread's } closes the tag
after the } of a switch block, a / starts a regex
after the } of a finally block, a / starts a regex
